Q: C implicit const casting (in dereferencing order) should be permitted but isn't A:

I'll take a stab at this.

adding consts in the order of dereferencing cannot generate issues; you're basically only restricting your access!

Does changing a pointer from object non_const * to object const * ever cause a change in the pointer encoding? Certainly implementations do not commonly do that, but could an implementation to that? Does C allow it?

If such a change is possible consider:
OP is not only trying to change a non-const pointer to const (clearly via the function call - thus allowing the compiler to adjust the pointer), but also wants the type of data it references to be treated the same (even though a pointer encoding change is needed), as the later code does not think the referenced pointers are non-const and doesn't convert them to const.

Perhaps C++ simply is not portable to such architectures and so will gladly convert object ** to const object * const *.

C, OTOH, was targeted to a very wide range of architectures. Many which are long gone.

Some embedded processors use use a Harvard architecture, and its variants, where true constant data lives in a different address space than typical object data and conversions to/from const data oblige some special handling. Perhaps that applies here?

what ... people do when a library function takes in a string array that it won't modify (?)

Cast, if the 2nd level object non-const * and object const * have the same encoding.

Q: How to obtain a table from an online pdf in R A:

Usually

X <- extract_tables("https://www.bankofgreece.gr/RelatedDocuments/NEW_INDEX_OF_APARTMENT_PRICES_BY_AGE.PDF")

should work, because extract_tables allows file to be A character string specifying the path or URL to a PDF file. but in this case, we receive an error probably due to the website detecting a script-download, because we did not pass any user-agent header.

In .rs.downloadFile(url = path, destfile = tmp, quiet = quiet, mode = "wb") : cannot open URL 'https://www.bankofgreece.gr/RelatedDocuments/NEW_INDEX_OF_APARTMENT_PRICES_BY_AGE.PDF': HTTP status was '403 Forbidden'

You can pass this user-agent header to httr::GET indicating human browsing and download the PDF successfully. If you extracted the table, you can unlink the temporary file.

library(tabulapdf)
library(httr)

tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf") 

httr::GET(
  "https://www.bankofgreece.gr/RelatedDocuments/NEW_INDEX_OF_APARTMENT_PRICES_BY_AGE.PDF",
  user_agent("Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36"),
  write_disk(tmp, overwrite = TRUE)
)

X <- tabulapdf::extract_tables(tmp)
unlink(tmp) # if you are done

Q: Payment Method Added but Dashboard Still Shows ‘Missing Valid Payment Method’ for WhatsApp API A:

I faced the same issue, but it got resolved for me now. The following are the steps I followed:

1. Although it says GST is optional but I see a message displaying to enter GST. We do not have a GST. Therefore, I simply entered the placeholder GST number that was given as an example. After clicking verify and save, the GST required message got disappeared. Although after a while it shows that "Your tax info couldn't be verified", but the GST required message is not showing up again. This way, work around for problem 1 worked for me.

2. The next problem is with the payment method. Credit cards didn't work for me. They were charged and added successfully, but template messages are failing with the same payment method error. Also, when I to the Meta Business Suite -> Settings -> WhatsApp accounts -> WhatsApp Manager -> Overview I saw a message that said "Missing Valid Payment method".

Adding the International Debit card worked for me. After adding the International debit card as the payment method, I waited for a couple of minutes and refreshed the Overview page in the WhatsApp manager. I observed the message "Missing Valid Payment method" disappeared. And my template messages are getting delivered via api successfully.
